title: Add read-only host-rules check for athena/records and main (D111, part
summary: Retry of job 20261024-033935-c4w4: add an athena-core module that GETs the rulesets view rules/branches/{branch} for athena/records and main and reports force-push forbidden, deletion forbidden and up-to-date required as in force, not in force, or unknown. Audience: Sri, who must set these host rules before the records cutover. The retry also fixes the earlier findings: the docs state the check sees rulesets only, the CHANGELOG cites §3 and §10, and the gate evidence cites the commands that ran.

defaults_applied.how: Fixture-based unit tests; cargo test and clippy clean.
Gate commands run and cited with output.
Criteria assert reported states from fixture replies and the GET-only calls, not file existence.
One new module plus registration and docs.
Doc comments cite D111 and the design section.
The doc now says rulesets only and the evidence cites commands, fixing the findings.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The typed request means redo the original check job; the introspection's proposed pre-handover evidence gate is a separate pipeline change and is not built here.
The user's correction stands: use GET repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch}, not the classic /protection endpoint (403 here).
Rules: non_fast_forward => force-push forbidden; deletion => deletion forbidden; required_status_checks with parameters.strict_required_status_checks_policy true => up-to-date required.
Runner errors or unparseable JSON give an 'unknown' state, never 'in force' or 'not in force'.
The check sees rulesets only; classic branch protection is not visible through this view.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: fixture replies in the rules/branches shape (JSON list of rule objects) give athena/records with non_fast_forward => force-push forbidden in force; deletion rule => deletion forbidden in force; main with required_status_checks whose strict_required_status_checks_policy is true => up-to-date required in force.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: tests assert `[]` reports all rules not in force; strict_required_status_checks_policy false or absent reports up-to-date not in force; a partial list (only non_fast_forward) reports force-push in force and deletion not in force.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a recording fake Runner test asserts only GET calls to `repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/athena/records` and `.../rules/branches/main`, with no method override and no field/body arguments, and no /protection call.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a runner error (403 or 5xx) or unparseable JSON makes the affected rules report unknown, not in force and not not-in-force.

The plain-text report names each of the three rules per branch and its state, e.g. 'athena/records: force-push forbidden: in force', so Sri can see which host rule to set; the report or module doc states that only rulesets are seen, not classic branch protection.

Module doc comments cite D111 and docs/design/records-history.md §3 and call this part 3 of job 1; the module is registered in crates/athena-core/src/lib.rs; the CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry cites both §3 and §10.

Run `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test` from the repo root: all exit 0 for the workspace. The producer's evidence for this criterion cites each command as run with its exit status and output tail.

out_of_scope: Changing any host setting or ruleset
The pre-handover evidence gate in the job pipeline
Wiring the check into a CLI command or the cutover flow
